# Use of AI in past, present and future outbreak modelling

## My view {.center}

::: {style="font-size: 1.25em; margin-top: 0.6em;"}
Many of these approaches are under-explored and not well integrated with
the rapidly evolving, noisy, sparse data settings I have worked in.
I am not aware of any real-world operational use so far, and I am mostly
not convinced by the evaluations.
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em; margin-top: 1em; color: #4a5899;"}
Sam Abbott, September 2026
:::

## Universal differential equations

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Keep the compartments. Replace the rate you cannot write down with a
  network fed by the data you have on behaviour, mobility and policy
- Philipps, Schmid and Hasenauer 2025. Noise and limited data degrade
  performance. The fitted mechanistic parameters did not match the
  published values
- Charlotte Holt, epiforecasts PhD student, is using UDEs to recover
  behavioural change in outbreaks to improve forecasts
- This is one answer to methods that cannot take the data sources that
  exist
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-seir-vs-ude.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Left, an SEIR box model with the transmission rate a random walk
and one arrow to a cases box. Right, the same SEIR boxes with the
transmission rate a neural network fed by mobility, surveys, policy,
weather and wastewater, and an arrow to cases, deaths and admissions."}

::: {.attribution}
Rackauckas et al. 2020, [arXiv:2001.04385](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.04385)
· Philipps, Schmid and Hasenauer 2025, npj Syst Biol Appl,
[PMC12398592](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12398592/)
· behaviour-informed UDEs for COVID-19 waves, Heliyon 2024
· Nina Schmid, epinowcast seminar, 4 March 2026,
[epinowcast.org](https://www.epinowcast.org/seminars/2026-03-04-nina-schmid/)

## Renewal as a neural network layer

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- A renewal process is a differentiable map from $R_t$ and past
  infections to today's infections. A layer, in network terms
- Stack them. Inputs to $R_t$, an $R_t$ layer, the renewal layer,
  observation layers, data streams. Gradients run back through all of it
- Swap the $R_t$ layer for a network on behaviour data and the rest of
  the model does not change
- The reuse across outbreaks we did not have, with the model structure
  kept
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-renewal-layer.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Five stacked boxes, inputs to Rt, an Rt layer, a renewal layer
with the renewal equation, observation layers and data streams, with
black forward arrows for simulation and dashed brick arrows back for
gradients of the log likelihood."}

::: {.attribution}
Composability with machine learning approaches, a design consideration
in the composable modelling grant, Abbott, Funk et al., research vision,
2026 · UDEs inside individual model components, EU grant idea note,
2026 · Pervez, Locatello and Gavves 2024, *Mechanistic Neural Networks*
:::
:::
::::

## AI-driven inference

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Simulate parameter and data pairs from any model you can run. Train a
  network to map data to a posterior. No likelihood needed
- OutbreakFlow, Radev et al. 2021. Generation time, undetected fraction
  and reporting delays for early COVID-19 in Germany
- Pinotti et al. 2025 fitted an SEIR model to the 2014 Sierra Leone
  Ebola data by neural posterior estimation. Jang, Candan and Chowell
  2026 compare it with ABC
- A way to fit the models flexible enough for the data
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-outbreakflow2021.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The OutbreakFlow architecture. A training phase on the left with
a prior, an SIRD model and simulated time series, a stack of filtering,
summary and inference networks in the middle producing an approximate
posterior, and an inference phase on the right taking observed time
series."}

::: {.attribution}
Figure 1 of Radev et al. 2021, PLOS Comput Biol,
[doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009472](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009472),
CC BY

· Jang, Candan and Chowell 2026, PLOS Comput Biol,
[doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014364](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014364)

## Foundation time series models

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Pretrained on many series from other domains. Your series in, a
  forecast out, no fitting
- Kalahasti et al. 2025. Strong short-term accuracy on sparse or
  irregular data. Wang, Li and Perra 2026. TabPFN-TS, zero-shot,
  rivalled the ECDC RespiCast ensemble on influenza-like illness
- Jafari et al. 2026. A mixture of pretrained forecasters did best on
  US influenza. CAPE pretrains on simulated epidemics
- An outbreak-specific foundation model that handles data changing over
  time is a project I would like to be involved in
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-foundation.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A stack of many grey time series labelled many series, many
domains, feeds a slate box labelled one pretrained model, a transformer,
which produces a brick forecast fan on a teal epidemic curve to the
right, labelled your series in, a forecast out, no fitting."}

::: {.attribution}
Kalahasti et al. 2025, medRxiv,

## Reinforcement learning for control

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Libin et al. 2020. School closure policies learned with PPO on a
  379-district influenza model of Great Britain
- Reymond et al. 2024. The Pareto front of multi-objective COVID-19
  mitigation policies on a Belgian stochastic compartmental model
- Bolshov and Chumachenko 2026, a scoping review of 13 studies. Limited
  prospective validation or real-world deployment testing
- Evaluation is the open problem here too
:::
